````text
# #3061: Patch: an Activate the game won't let you use says why, and the fuzz holds every ability to it
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

Some cards on the field have an Activate button. When the ability can't be used because it needs a target you don't have, the button is greyed out and says only "Not now". Job Application's "send a card from your hand" with an empty hand is one example. A card in your hand that can't be played already tells you why; abilities on the field were left out. Once this is built, the button names the real reason, and the nightly random-game checks catch any ability that is greyed out without one.

## Why

- `crates/engine/src/subsystems/activate.rs:1101-1102` promises that `usable` "is exactly whether `legal_actions` lists it". But `activation_views_for` (:1124-1137) sets `usable` and `reason` from `why_cannot_activate_ability` alone, which reads no targets.
- `activate_actions_for` (:685-716) also drops an ability whose required targets are missing (`play_choice_combinations`) or whose discards can't be paid (R450, R682). Such an ability is not listed, yet its view says `usable: true` and gives no `reason`.
- Job Application has a required hand target (`crates/cards/src/scripts/stinkyscape/c112_job_application.rs:355`). Its test `entering_opens_stage_1_and_an_empty_hand_has_nothing_to_send` (:586-604) asserts that the Activate is not listed. Nothing checks its view.
- `apps/web/src/game/ActivateControl.tsx:137`: a control that is not legal shows `activation.reason ?? NOT_NOW`, so the player reads "Not now".
- R2975000 (issue #2975) closed the same gap for hand cards and added monitor check I13 (`crates/engine/src/testkit/invariants.rs:47`, :967). Activations have no such check.

## Proposal

- `activation_views_for` sets `usable` from the listing: whether `activate_actions_for` offers at least one action for the ability. When it offers none, `reason` comes from the refusal `reduce` gives the ability's first choice, as R2975000 does for plays, so the view and the listing can't drift apart.
- A monitor check beside I13, reading I6's existing view and listing so it costs no extra view or listing. For each `ActivationView` the viewer may use, `usable` holds exactly when an activation of that ability is listed, and `reason` exactly when it is not.
- A ruling note in its issue's block, naming R384 and R2975000, with its proving tests and its §11 paragraph in `spec/pending/<issue>.md`.

## Where it lands

- `crates/engine/src/subsystems/activate.rs` and `crates/engine/src/testkit/invariants.rs`.
- `crates/engine/tests/rules/`: a fixture ability with a required target.
- The tests of `crates/cards/src/scripts/stinkyscape/c112_job_application.rs`.
- §10.8, `spec/rulings/` and `spec/pending/`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Job Application with an empty hand: its view has `usable: false` and a `reason`.
- [ ] Rules tests with a fixture ability whose required target is missing, and one whose discards can't be paid: neither is usable, and each has a reason.
- [ ] A monitor unit test on a doctored view (usable but not listed) reports exactly one finding of the new check.
- [ ] `cargo jackioh fuzz --seeds 200` and its `--handicap` wave stay green.
- [ ] `cargo jackioh golden check` passes, or the pull request explains its diff.
- [ ] `cargo jackioh spec check` passes.

## Size and risks

Medium: about 5 files and 250 lines with tests. Label it hard, since it touches engine rules. It changes `viewFor` for the affected abilities, so the golden fold and the web's readers of `data-usable` need checking. A real ability the new check flags turns the fuzz red until it is fixed.

_Written by `claude-4` (claude, `sonnet`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/41930431328)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

An ability on the field that `legalActions` does not list now has `usable: false` and a `reason`, so the Activate button says why instead of "Not now". Job Application's "send a card from your hand" with an empty hand is the example. `usable` comes from the listing itself (`activate_actions_for`). The `reason` is `why_cannot_activate_ability`'s refusal when that fires, and otherwise the refusal `reduce` gives the ability's first choice. A new monitor check, I14, holds every `ActivationView` to the listing, and its ruling is R3061000. It changes no state, event, replay or AI decision.

## Files to touch

| File | | What |
|---|---|---|
| `crates/engine/src/subsystems/activate.rs` | change | Split `activate_actions_for` into a per-ability `offered_actions`. Add `why_no_action_listed`. Rewrite `usable` and `reason` in `activation_views_for`. Update its doc comment. |

| `crates/engine/tests/rules/activate.rs` | change | New `mod r3061000_…` with the engine tests. Add `activation_views_for` and `pairer` to the imports. |
| `crates/cards/src/scripts/stinkyscape/c112_job_application.rs` | change | One new test in `mod tests`. |
| `crates/tools/src/fuzz.rs` | change | Header comment: I1–I14. |
| `crates/tools/README.md` | change | The `fuzz` row names I14. |
| `spec/rulings/R3061000.md` | new | The ruling note. |

| `spec/10-engine-guide.md` | change | §10.8: the bullet "The cards' own state" and the `playReason` paragraph. |

Governing notes: §10.2, §10.5 step 1, §10.8, R384, R90, R450, R682, R703, R979000, R2975000, R1865000, CLAUDE.md rules 3, 4 and 7.

Do not touch:
- `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`, `.claude/`.
- `apps/web`. The view's shape is unchanged and `ActivateControl.tsx:137` already reads `reason`.

## Steps

1. **`activate.rs`, `activate_actions_for` (about line 689).** Keep its signature and doc comment.
   - Body: `for decl in abilities_of(state, card) { if why_cannot_activate_ability(state, player, &card.id, Some(&decl.id)).is_err() { continue; } out.extend(offered_actions(state, player, card, &decl)); }`.
   - Directly below it add `fn offered_actions(state: &GameState, player: PlayerId, card: &CardInstance, decl: &ActivationDecl) -> Vec<ActivateAction>`.
   - Move the old loop body into it unchanged: `tribute_sets`, `choices`, the two `for` loops, the R450/R682 discard `continue`, the `pushed` struct and the R1200 dedupe. Its doc comment is "R384, R3061000: what one ability that passed `why_cannot_activate_ability` offers: each Tribute set crossed with each choice combination whose targets' discards the hand can pay."
   - Because `decl` is now a reference, change `&decl` to `decl` in `tribute_units_for`, `discards_owed` and `declared_of`. `decl.cost`, `decl.id` and `decl.targets` stay as they are.
   - The order and contents of the listing must not change. Existing seeds and the AI depend on that order.

2. **`activate.rs`, new `fn why_no_action_listed(state, player, card, decl) -> Option<String>`**, placed after `offered_actions`. It runs only when the ability passed `why_cannot_activate_ability` and `offered_actions` is empty.
   - Doc: "R3061000: the refusal `reduce` gives the ability's first choice."
   - Compute `tributes`: `unit_sets(&tribute_units_for(state, player, card, decl), decl.cost.and_then(|cost| cost.tribute).unwrap_or(0).max(0)).into_iter().next().filter(|set| !set.is_empty())`.
   - Compute `picks: Vec<(Option<Vec<Selection>>, Option<Vec<String>>)>` from `play_choice_combinations(state, player, card, Some(&declared_of(decl)))`, mapping each `choice` to `(choice.targets, choice.modes)`.
   - If `picks` is empty, no combination exists: a required pick the board cannot answer (R703). Push one probe, `(None, modes)`, where `modes` is the first option of each of `decl.modes` (`filter_map(|mode| mode.options.first().cloned())`), and `modes` is `None` when `decl.modes` is empty. That makes `refuse_targets` give the "cannot be played without N legal target(s)" refusal.
   - For each pick, build `ActivateAction { instance_id: card.id.clone(), ability: Some(decl.id.clone()), tributes: tributes.clone(), targets, modes }` and call `why_activate_refused(state, player, &action)`.
   - On `Ok(())`, return `None`. On `Err(error)`, keep the first message with `refusal.get_or_insert(error.message)`. After the loop return `refusal`.
   - Do not write a second copy of the discard or Tribute filters. Put each combination to `why_activate_refused`, as R2975000 does for plays.

3. **`activate.rs`, `activation_views_for`.** Replace the `reason` and `usable` lines in the `.map(|decl| …)` closure (`decl` is `&ActivationDecl` there) with:
   ```rust
   let gate = why_cannot_activate_ability(state, viewer, &card.id, Some(&decl.id)).err().map(|e| e.message);
   let listed = gate.is_none() && !offered_actions(state, viewer, card, decl).is_empty();
   let reason = if listed { None } else { gate.or_else(|| why_no_action_listed(state, viewer, card, decl)) };
   ```
   - Keep `uses_left` as it is. Set `usable: listed, reason`.
   - Update the doc comment: "`usable` is whether the listing offers an `activate` of it; `reason` says why not (R3061000)."
   - Compute `usable` from the listing, not from `reason.is_none()`. If the listing and the reducer ever drift apart, the view must stay honest so I14 can see it.

4. **`invariants.rs`, I14.** Add `ActivationView` and `BackrowView` to the `use crate::wire::{…}` list, then add this function after `play_reason_violations`:
   `pub fn activation_reason_violations(state: &GameState, viewer: PlayerId, view: &PlayerView, legal: &[ActionBody]) -> Vec<String>`
   - **Window.** Return `Vec::new()` unless the seat may act, using the same condition as I13: `state.result.is_none() && state.phase == Phase::Main && state.pending.is_none() && state.active == viewer`. Outside it, the refusal is `why_cannot_activate_ability`'s own.
   - **Listing.** `listed: IndexSet<(&str, &str)>` from `legal`, taking `ActionBody::Activate { instance_id, ability: Some(ability), .. }`.
   - **Views.** For `side in [&view.you, &view.opponent]`, collect `(instance_id, def_id, &ActivationView)` from each `side.units.iter().flatten()` unit's `activations.iter().flatten()`. Do the same for each `side.backrow.iter().flatten()` slot that is `BackrowView::Public(card)`. Skip `carried`: the listing never walks it.
   - **One finding per ability.** For each, match `(activation.usable, listed.contains(&(instance_id, ability)), activation.reason.as_deref())`:
     - `(true, false, _)` gives `"I14 usable but unlisted: …"`
     - `(false, true, _)` gives `"I14 listed but unusable: …"`
     - `(false, false, None)` gives `"I14 silent ability: …"`
     - `(true, true, Some(reason))` gives `"I14 stray reason: … \"{reason}\" …"`
     - anything else: `continue`.
   - **Message shape.** Lead with the id, then the viewer, `def_id`, `instance_id`, ability and `state.turn`, and end with `(§10.8, R384, R3061000)`.
   - **Wiring.** In `InvariantMonitor::hidden` (about line 2751), add `violations.extend(activation_reason_violations(state, viewer, &view, &legal));` after the I13 line. It reuses I6's view and listing, so it adds no cost.

9. **`spec/rulings/R3061000.md`** (new), modeled on `R2975000.md`.

10. **`spec/pending/3061.md`** (new): one paragraph, `**[[R3061000]] <title> (issue #3061, 2026-11-04)**: …`, ending "It takes R3061000, the first number of issue #3061's block, and edits [[§10.8]]." Follow `spec/pending/2975.md`.

## Tests

All engine tests are in `crates/engine/tests/rules/activate.rs`, mod `r3061000_an_activate_that_is_not_listed_says_why`. Use `playing(seed)`, `put(&mut state, &pairer.id, slot(P1, Row::Backrow, 1), json!({}))`, `put(&mut state, &ghost.id, slot(P2, Row::Units, lane), json!({}))`, `state.players.p1.hand = Vec::new()` and `in_hand(&mut state, &sentry.id, P1, n)`. Read the view with `activation_views_for(&state, P1, card(&state, &id)).unwrap()`.

1. `r3061000_a_required_target_the_board_cannot_answer_is_unusable_and_says_why`

2. `r3061000_discards_the_hand_cannot_pay_together_make_it_unusable_and_say_why`

3. `r3061000_discards_the_hand_can_pay_list_the_ability_and_say_nothing`
   - Same board with a hand of 4.
   - Asserts: `activate_actions_for` has len 1, `usable == true`, `reason == None`.

4. `r3061000_i14_reports_exactly_one_finding_for_a_view_that_disagrees_with_the_listing`
   - On test 2's state with `view_for` and `legal_actions`, `activation_reason_violations(&state, P1, &view, &legal)` is empty. `create_invariant_monitor(&state).hidden(&state)` has no finding starting with "I14".
   - Doctor `usable = true` on the pairer's view in `view.you.backrow` (find the `BackrowView::Public` card): exactly one finding, starting "I14 usable but unlisted", containing the instance id and "R3061000".
   - Doctor `reason = None`: exactly one, "I14 silent ability".
   - On test 3's state, doctor `usable = false`: one, "I14 listed but unusable". Doctor `reason = Some("stray".into())`: one, "I14 stray reason".
   - With `theirs.active = P2` (as in `play_reason.rs`), the doctored view gives no findings.

5. In `c112_job_application.rs`: `r3061000_upload_resume_with_an_empty_hand_is_unusable_and_says_why`.
   - Build the scenario of `entering_opens_stage_1_and_an_empty_hand_has_nothing_to_send` and call `played(&mut s, None)`.
   - `activation_views_for(s.state(), P1, s.card(ID))` has len 1 (`ANSWER` is closed at Stage 1), `ability == SEND`, `usable == false`, `reason == Some("Job Application cannot be played without a legal target")`.
   - With a card in hand (`setup("ja-r3061000", false, &[])` then `played`), the view has `usable == true` and `reason == None`.

- [ ] Job Application with an empty hand: view `usable: false` and a `reason` (test 5).
- [ ] A fixture ability with a missing required target, and one with unpayable discards: neither usable, each with a reason (tests 1 and 2).

- [ ] `spec check` passes. `R3061000.md` and `spec/pending/3061.md` exist. `spec/11-rulings.md` and `spec/INDEX.md` are untouched.

- [ ] The engine and cards tests pass.

## Risks

- **Listing order.** `legal_actions` order feeds the AI, replay and fuzz seeds. Step 1 keeps the order (ability, then Tribute set, then choice) exactly.
- **Existing tests that assert `usable`.** Some may have encoded the old behaviour. Candidates are `starship.rs:591`, `starscape.rs:96`, `c148_alteran_reach.rs:125` and `weapon_kit.rs`. If one fails, check whether the ability really lists nothing. Fix the test only if R3061000 and the reducer agree, and record why.
- **A fuzz I14 finding.** It means the listing and the view drifted. Fix the cause in the engine. Do not narrow I14, and never add an `#[allow]` or skip.
- **View cost.** `view_for` now builds the ability's choice combinations, as `legal_actions` does. R90 bounds them at 64, and only abilities past `why_cannot_activate_ability` pay.
- **Hidden information.** Reasons name only the viewer's own card, public units and counts of the viewer's own hand, as R979000 argues. I6 still runs.
- **ts-rs.** Do not edit `wire/view.rs`. Any diff in `apps/web/src/wire/` fails the cargo-tests check.
- **Spec check.** Every `R3061000` cited in code needs the note. Rust test names need the token `r3061000`. Rule 8 flags the word "ruling" in §2–§10 text without a `[[R…]]` link.

## Open questions

None block the build. The decisions to record:
- **Reason wording.** An Activate's reason uses step 1's words, so a missing required pick reads "…cannot be played without a legal target". I rejected activation-specific wording because `refuse_targets` is shared with plays, whose words R979000 and R2975000 hold fixed. A person may want nicer wording later.
- **Monitor window.** I14 uses I13's window (the seat may act) and reads `units` and `backrow` only. I rejected checking every state, since out of the window both sides give `why_cannot_activate_ability`'s own refusal.
- **Test placement.** All engine tests go in `activate.rs`, not a new module file, which avoids choosing among the three `rules` binaries.
- **Ruling number.** R3061000 is the first number in issue #3061's block.
````

   - Directly below it add `fn offered_actions(state: &GameState, player: PlayerId, card: &CardInstance, decl: &ActivationDecl) -> Vec<ActivateAction>`.
   - Move the old loop body into it unchanged: `tribute_sets`, `choices`, the two `for` loops, the R450/R682 discard `continue`, the `pushed` struct and the R1200 dedupe. Its doc comment is "R384, R3061000: what one ability that passed `why_cannot_activate_ability` offers: each Tribute set crossed with each choice combination whose targets' discards the hand can pay."
   - Because `decl` is now a reference, change `&decl` to `decl` in `tribute_units_for`, `discards_owed` and `declared_of`. `decl.cost`, `decl.id` and `decl.targets` stay as they are.
   - The order and contents of the listing must not change. Existing seeds and the AI depend on that order.

2. **`activate.rs`, new `fn why_no_action_listed(state, player, card, decl) -> Option<String>`**, placed after `offered_actions`. It runs only when the ability passed `why_cannot_activate_ability` and `offered_actions` is empty.
   - Doc: "R3061000: the refusal `reduce` gives the ability's first choice."
   - Compute `tributes`: `unit_sets(&tribute_units_for(state, player, card, decl), decl.cost.and_then(|cost| cost.tribute).unwrap_or(0).max(0)).into_iter().next().filter(|set| !set.is_empty())`.
   - Compute `picks: Vec<(Option<Vec<Selection>>, Option<Vec<String>>)>` from `play_choice_combinations(state, player, card, Some(&declared_of(decl)))`, mapping each `choice` to `(choice.targets, choice.modes)`.
   - If `picks` is empty, no combination exists: a required pick the board cannot answer (R703). Push one probe, `(None, modes)`, where `modes` is the first option of each of `decl.modes` (`filter_map(|mode| mode.options.first().cloned())`), and `modes` is `None` when `decl.modes` is empty.    - Do not write a second copy of the discard or Tribute filters. Put each combination to `why_activate_refused`, as R2975000 does for plays.

   ```rust
   let gate = why_cannot_activate_ability(state, viewer, &card.id, Some(&decl.id)).err().map(|e| e.message);
   ```

   - **Window.** Return `Vec::new()` unless the seat may act, using the same condition as I13: `state.result.is_none() && state.phase == Phase::Main && state.pending.is_none() && state.active == viewer`. Outside it, the refusal is `why_cannot_activate_ability`'s own.
   - **Listing.** `listed: IndexSet<(&str, &str)>` from `legal`, taking `ActionBody::Activate { instance_id, ability: Some(ability), .. }`.
   - **Views.** For `side in [&view.you, &view.opponent]`, collect `(instance_id, def_id, &ActivationView)` from each `side.units.iter().flatten()` unit's `activations.iter().flatten()`. Do the same for each `side.backrow.iter().flatten()` slot that is `BackrowView::Public(card)`. Skip `carried`: the listing never walks it.
   - **One finding per ability.** For each, match `(activation.usable, listed.contains(&(instance_id, ability)), activation.reason.as_deref())`:
     - `(true, false, _)` gives `"I14 usable but unlisted: …"`
     - `(false, true, _)` gives `"I14 listed but unusable: …"`
     - `(false, false, None)` gives `"I14 silent ability: …"`
     - `(true, true, Some(reason))` gives `"I14 stray reason: … \"{reason}\" …"`
     - anything else: `continue`.
   - **Message shape.** Lead with the id, then the viewer, `def_id`, `instance_id`, ability and `state.turn`, and end with `(§10.8, R384, R3061000)`.
   - **Wiring.** In `InvariantMonitor::hidden` (about line 2751), add `violations.extend(activation_reason_violations(state, viewer, &view, &legal));` after the I13 line. It reuses I6's view and listing, so it adds no cost.
   - **Doc comments** (builder checks each by reading it):
     - "The thirteen checks" becomes "The fourteen checks".
     - A
